questions.prompt: A sensor driver publishes with best_effort reliability. Your subscriber requests reliable. What happens?
options: They do not connect: no data and no exception in your code.
The subscriber receives the data with retransmissions.
The publisher is upgraded to reliable automatically.
questions.explanation: A best-effort offer cannot satisfy a reliable request.

questions.prompt: Messages arrive every 25 ms and the callback takes 40 ms. Utilization S/P. Precision 0.01.
Overloaded keep-last queue, depth 6, arrivals every 10 ms. Upper bound on queueing delay (ms).
Long-run fraction of messages dropped when utilization is 1.25 (single worker). Precision 0.01.
A map is published once at startup. A planner starting later must still receive it. Which QoS on both ends?
options: best_effort, transient_local on the publisher only
questions.explanation: transient_local on both sides keeps and replays the last sample.

questions.prompt: A 150 ms callback and a 100 ms safety timer share one single-threaded executor. What is the effect?
options: The timer can fire late because only one callback runs at a time.
The timer fires twice as fast, because the executor catches up on missed ticks.
The 150 ms callback is skipped whenever the 100 ms timer becomes due.
Nothing happens; timers have a dedicated thread that is independent of callbacks.
questions.explanation: Callbacks are serialized in a single-threaded executor.

questions.prompt: A perception node must publish at 30 Hz but its subscriber sees 12 Hz and stale data. Describe how you would diagnose it with numbers and what you would change.
rubric: Measures callback time and arrival period and computes utilization.
Checks QoS (depth, reliability) and the executor/callback groups with ros2 topic info and logs.
Proposes a fix: faster callback, decimation, smaller depth, separate callback group or executor, with a re-measurement.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
